author_attribution_notes: Keep Alexey’s first-person framing only for actions and observations explicitly present in the supplied source; preserve attribution to DataTalks.Club, AI Shipping Labs, and other projects where named.

required_facts.fact: I have a lot of projects that I started with some grand idea, spent time on, and then never really did anything with.
Some of them work, but I don’t need them anymore.
Some turned out to be more complex than I expected, or I couldn’t build them the way I imagined.
I abandoned many of them at different stages.
My GitHub profile shows 195 repositories, and that’s only my personal account.
I also experiment with projects in the DataTalks.Club and AI Shipping Labs organizations on GitHub.
With coding agents, I write a lot more code than ever before, because I can try ideas faster.
Naturally, I also create more projects that don’t go anywhere.

My GitHub profile page showing 195 repositories

But I don’t think this is a problem.
These projects may not reach their final form, and I may not use them afterward, but building them still teaches me something.
Some help me understand how to work with coding assistants.
Others help me think through a vague problem in practice.
